title: Lists Practice
subject: Computer Science · Introduction to AI
instructions: Answer the three questions about lists. Use the hints if you get stuck. Your teacher will review your work.

questions.prompt: What number does this program print?

misconceptions.note: 3 is the index of the last item. len counts the items.

hints: What does len() count? Read the list and think about what it measures.
Count the items between the square brackets, one at a time.
A similar problem: len(["a", "b"]) is 2, because there are two items. Now count the pets.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? Type the numbers separated by spaces.
questions.code:
nums = [10, 20, 30]
nums.append(40)
for n in nums:
    print(n)

misconceptions.note: Look again at nums.append(40). What happens to the list?

hints: Check the list before the loop runs. What does append do to it?
append adds an item to the end. Write out the list after that line, then follow the loop.
A similar problem: [1, 2] with append(3) becomes [1, 2, 3], and the loop prints 1, 2, 3. Try the same steps.

questions.prompt: What index does the first item of a list have?

misconceptions.note: Everyday counting starts at 1, but Python starts at 0.

hints: Look back at the lesson section about indexes.
In everyday counting we start at 1. Does Python do the same?
A similar problem: in ["x", "y"], which index gives "x"? Think about how the lesson numbers items.
